title: Stop count_from reciting its own answers
problem: Every count_from instruction in both draws states the three answers before the child responds ("Start at 3, then say 4, 5, 6"). The item is unanswerable as assessment; the child hears or reads the key.
mechanism: Authored into the easy support tier: service/math/gemini-number-sequencer.ts:133 tells Gemini the instruction should "model the first step (e.g. 'Start at 3, then say 4, 5, 6…')", which models all three continuation values. The contract (docs/contracts/number-sequencer.md:86-87) exempts count-from from the oracle answer-leak rule because "the visible terms ARE the stimulus", so nothing catches it. Every probe ran at difficulty=easy.
proposal: Rewrite the easy-tier line to model ONE step at most ("Start at 3, then say 4… keep going"); add a post-parse validator that rejects any count-from item whose instruction, hint or narration contains every correctAnswers value; refresh the contract so the START term is the stimulus and the continuation values fall under the answer-leak rule.
acceptance: Three fresh draws of COUNT001-01-I at easy, medium and hard with zero instructions containing all of correctAnswers; the math-k content check "instruction does not recite the answers" passes on every item after --redraw; /oracle-test number-sequencer count_from answer-leak rule green.

title: Let a K ordinal objective reach tenth — FIXED 2026-09-08
problem: CLOSED 2026-09-08 (slice 3), confirmed on the 2026-09-09 redraw: maxPosition 10, ten characters, targets sixth through tenth in both draws. Original: COUNT001-04-D named sixth through tenth; both draws returned one challenge with maxPosition 5 targeting fifth.
mechanism: The objective window resolver exists (gemini-ordinal-line.ts:355-372 reads "6th through 10th"), but gradeMaxPosition() returns 5 for K (line 372) and the window is clamped to it twice: the resolver clamps end to the grade ceiling, and the validator clamps again (line 495 `if K && maxPosition > 5 → 5`; line 509 Math.min(gradeMaxPosition, …)). So the window can never lift a K line past fifth. Nothing enforces a minimum item count.
proposal: Treat the grade as the DEFAULT, not the ceiling, when the objective names a window: let an explicit window raise maxPosition to MAX_POSITION (10) at K; drop the line-495 clamp for windowed lessons; emit at least three challenges targeting positions inside the window; keep the four-clue hold for build_sequence by pre-filling part of the line.
acceptance: Two fresh draws of COUNT001-04-D with maxPosition 10, at least three items, targets that include positions 6-10, and names free of numbers; COUNT001-04-A still draws first-fifth on a 5-long line (no regression of the K default).

title: Route the missing difference and honor the tier preference
problem: OPS001-02-F names a missing difference OR minuend. All sixteen missing_number items across two draws hide the minuend; the easy tier declares a preference for the count-on position (operand2) that never appears.
mechanism: missing_number is defined as operand1/operand2 only, never the result (gemini-math-fact-fluency.ts:46), so the missing-DIFFERENCE half is equation_solve by design, not a defect: the review now pairs both modes. The residual is real: resolveSupportStructure sets unknownPositionPref = operand2 for easy (line 148) but every easy item came back operand1, so the preference is not reaching the generated set.
proposal: Trace unknownPositionPref from the tier resolver into the prompt/schema and post-parse; at easy, alternate operand2 and operand1 so the session holds both forms; leave result-unknown to equation_solve.
acceptance: Two fresh easy draws with operand2 present and all equations true within 10; an equation_solve draw of the same objective yields difference-unknown items.

title: Make each challenge a different problem — FIXED 2026-09-08
target: comparison-builder / compare_groups; number-sequencer / fill_missing; hundreds-chart / highlight_sequence
problem: fill_missing put the blank in the second slot on every item and repeated 1,_,3,4 up to three times per session; hundreds-chart repeated the identical by-5-from-5 highlight five times in one draw; compare_groups returned the same five comparisons for two objectives and two draws.
mechanism: comparison-builder: the tier resolver fixes only the count GAP (gemini-comparison-builder.ts:234, easy gap 3-6) and leaves the counts to Gemini, which converges on the same obvious pairs (5v1, 1v4, 3v3, 1v5). number-sequencer: Gemini places the blanks and copies the prompt example shape (line 47-50), so the blank lands in slot two and sequences repeat. hundreds-chart: startNumber is always the skipValue (line 556) and the grade-1 pool is [2,5,10] (line 355), so with a named pool of two values, seven challenges must repeat, and the extra 10 drifts in from the band pool.
proposal: comparison-builder: run /add-number-pool-service so code pre-rolls the two counts inside the objective range with the tier gap and a guaranteed equal case. number-sequencer: Gemini emits complete sequences; code chooses the blank index round-robin and rejects duplicate sequences (ask 7, ship 5). hundreds-chart: when the objective names skip values, the pool is those values only; enumerate distinct (skip, start, givenCount) problems and cap the session at the distinct count instead of repeating.
acceptance: Two fresh draws where every fill_missing line is unique and blanks cover at least three positions; every hundreds-chart challenge is a distinct skip/start pair within 2s and 5s; two compare_groups draws differ in at least three comparisons while still including equal. MET 2026-09-08 (live /api/lumina/eval-test draws, 2 per generator): fill_missing 5/5 distinct windows and 5/5 distinct blank slots in both draws; hundreds-chart 2 challenges from the pool [2,5] with no by-10s and no repeat; compare_groups 5/5 distinct pairs in each of 5 draws, one equal case per session, K counts inside 1-10. Tests: 20 new across three .variety.test.ts files.

title: Keep compare_groups inside the objective's range — FIXED 2026-09-09
problem: Found on the 2026-09-09 full redraw: after slice 4 the pooled counts vary, but they are rolled over the K band (1-10) rather than the objective's window. COUNT001-03-A and MEAS001-02-B both name groups of UP TO 5; 7 of 10 and 6 of 10 comparisons exceed it (5v9, 10v4, 3v8).
mechanism: The slice-4 pool service anchors compare_groups counts on the grade band (createNumberPool with the band's 1-10) and applies the tier gap; nothing reads the objective's stated ceiling. The same objective-window axis slice 3 added to ordinal-line and the scene is the missing input. Pattern to copy (slice 7, gemini-counting-board.ts): `boundIn` / `scopeCeiling` read "to N" / "within N" from topic and intent, take the min against the grade-band ceiling, and every code-owned draw is clamped to it. A prompt-only bound never reaches numbers that code picks after the call.
proposal: Feed the objective number window ("up to 5", "6-10") into the pool anchors so both counts stay inside it; keep the tier gap and the guaranteed equal case; fall back to the band only when the objective names no window.
acceptance: Fresh draws of COUNT001-03-A with every count in 1-5 and of COUNT001-03-B with every count in 6-10, each with an equal case and no repeated pair; a K draw with no window keeps 1-10. MET 2026-09-09 (real generations driven through geminiService, the dev server being wedged by a concurrent session): COUNT001-03-A ×2 and MEAS001-02-B every count in 1-5; COUNT001-03-B easy and medium every count in 6-10; all five draws 5/5 distinct pairs with one equal case; a K draw naming no range still spans 1-10. The window is read by the SHARED resolveScopeRange micro-call (schema, not regex — it reads the 6-10 FLOOR a ceiling-only parse cannot); the tier gap refits when a narrow window cannot supply five distinct pairs. Tests: 7 new in gemini-comparison-builder.variety.test.ts (14 total).

title: Frame a marked day as today
problem: TIME001-02-B asks for today's day of the week; both draws ask which weekday an arbitrary 2025 date falls on and slip in first-Monday pattern questions. The mechanics are sound but the framing misses the objective.
mechanism: identify is defined as date lookup ("What date is the third Wednesday?", service/calendar/gemini-calendar-explorer.ts:22) and the component has no notion of today: it only highlights highlightDates (CalendarExplorer.tsx:36, 291). There is no field the generator could set to mark a day as today.
proposal: Add todayDate to the identify schema and a "Today" marker on that cell in CalendarExplorer; when the objective names today/yesterday/tomorrow, the prompt asks relative to the marked day; keep plain date lookups for objectives that name dates.
acceptance: Fresh draws of TIME001-02-B/C where every question references the marked today (and yesterday/tomorrow for 02-C) with a consistent key; the Today marker is visible before the question is asked.

title: Stabilize per-draw yield and bins
problem: One sorting-station draw collapsed hot/warm/cold to two bins in all four challenges while the other produced all three; one compare-objects draw returned two items and the other seven.
mechanism: sorting-station derives maxCategories from whatever Gemini returned (gemini-sorting-station.ts:1223 Math.max(config ?? 2, …)) and never reads the categories the objective names, so a two-bin draw is accepted. compare-objects ships min(count, returned) (gemini-compare-objects.ts:873) with no minimum and no regeneration.
proposal: sorting-station: resolve the named categories from the objective text (schema, not regex) and reject a draw missing one of them; compare-objects: ask count+2, ship count, enforce a minimum of three and regenerate once when short.
acceptance: Three consecutive draws each with all three temperature bins present and at least three attribute items per session.

title: K sorting draws need a full round count and an emoji that matches its label
problem: CLOSED 2026-09-09. Both faults were code, and each had a second cap behind it. YIELD: the orchestrator hardcoded 4 challenges regardless of the ask, and sort_variety capped rounds at 3 — so a 5-round lesson could not be served at all. It now honours config.challengeCount (2-10, default 4), and rounds past 3 come from ANOTHER on-topic object set rather than a fourth axis forced onto one (an observed draw sorted elephant/mouse/dog/horse by "Tall/Round"); axisRank spends a set on category/type/size before shape/color. A third cap sat below both: the keep-or-drop speakability gate runs AFTER generation, so every dropped challenge came out of the lesson and left an id gap (c1/c2/c3/c5) — single-mode sessions now generate count+2 and trim after the gate. EMOJI: cardPictureFault faults a card whose picture is a known one and whose label names a known noun it does not depict, with no other word agreeing ("Red Banana" 🍓 goes; "Red Apple" 🍎 and "Rain Hat" 👒 stay). Wired into the sort family, two_attributes (which had NO draw gate at all), and sort-variety, where the SET is rejected because dropping one shared card thins it below the band object floor. Evidence: 2 fresh K draws per mode at count=5 — 5/5 every time, contiguous ids, every card agreeing; 14/14 unit including a negative case driving the reported card through the real path. Contract R11 + R12 added; R12 amends R1's sort_variety probe (the set stays constant WITHIN a set, not across the lesson). Residual: two_attributes draw 1 asked "need + food" all five times — variety of the compound criterion is untouched and pre-existing.
mechanism: Both are draw-quality faults, not band faults: the floors came down on the reading axis and these survive it. The yield shortfall is the distinctness/top-up pattern slice 4 addressed elsewhere (ask count+2, ship count, deterministic backfill); the emoji mismatch needs a label/emoji agreement check in the same place `hasPicture` already rejects text fragments in `gemini-sorting-station.ts`. Draws: qa/reader-fit/k-band-floor-2026-09-08.md.
proposal: Ask for count+2 rounds and reject duplicates so `sort_variety` ships the count the lesson asked for; extend the existing picture gate so a card whose label names a different object than its emoji depicts is discarded before the child sees it.
acceptance: Two fresh K draws per mode at the asked-for count, with every card's emoji agreeing with its label.
